SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالقبائلوالأحياءوماي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالقبائلوالأحياءوماي.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالقبائلوالأحياءوماي.claim: Thamud and Saba can denote either a tribe lineage or a living community; Sībawayh cites Qur'anic forms of both names as evidence for these uses.

ITQAN:v2p364/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p364/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p364/r11.claim: كأن لم يغنوا means as though they had never existed; Labid's phrase غنيت سبتا is cited as evidence.
ITQAN:v2p364/r11.anchor: قال كأن لم يكونوا أما سمعت قول لبيد

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Ṣayḥah means a roar and describes the destruction of Thamūd by thunder and lightning; the masculine verb follows the intended meaning rather than the feminine noun.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The wor  ﺻﻴﺤﺔ means “roar.” It refers to the punishment that descended on the Thamūd

STUDYQURAN:11:67/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:67/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:67/r2.claim: The cited commentary explains why morning found them lifeless as if they had never lived there; the wording recurs in 11:94–95.
STUDYQURAN:11:67/r2.anchor: which explains why morning found them lying lifeless in their abode, as though they had never dwelt there (see the identical wording in vv. 94–95; cf. 7:78).

TAB-FULL:v12p465/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r1.claim: The cry struck those who wrongfully hamstrung God's she-camel and disbelieved; death left them motionless in their courtyards, as though they had never lived there.

TAB-FULL:v12p465/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r3.claim: The phrase means they had not lived or dwelt there; al-Tabari notes he has already established this meaning with evidence.
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r3.anchor: كأن لم يعيشوا فيها، ولم يعمروا بها

TAB-FULL:v12p465/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as if they had never lived there.
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله " {كأن لم يغنوا فيها} [الأعراف: 92] كأن لم يعيشوا فيها "

TAB-FULL:v12p465/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r5.claim: Qatada gives the same gloss: as if they had never lived there.
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r5.anchor: حدثنا بشر، قال: ثنا يزيد، قال: ثنا سعيد، عن قتادة، مثله

TAB-FULL:v12p465/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r6.claim: Thamud disbelieved in their Lord by denying His signs.
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r6.anchor: ألا إن ثمود كفروا بآيات ربهم فجحدوها

TAB-FULL:v12p465/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r7.claim: The curse asks that Allah put Thamud far away through the punishment that descended on them.
TAB-FULL:v12p465/r7.anchor: ألا أبعد الله ثمود لنزول العذاب بهم

TABATABAI:11:65-68/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:65-68/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:65-68/r9.claim: “Yaghnaw” means they had dwelt there; the pronoun refers to their dwellings.
TABATABAI:11:65-68/r9.anchor: غني بالمكان أي أقام فيه، والضمير راجع إلى الديار

TABATABAI:11:65-68/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:65-68/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:65-68/r10.claim: The two closing clauses summarize the detailed story: the first its outcome for Thamūd and Salih’s mission, the second God’s recompense, paralleling the close of Hūd’s story.
TABATABAI:11:65-68/r10.anchor: فالجملة الأولى تلخيص ما انتهى إليه أمر ثمود ودعوة صالح عليه السلام

TABATABAI:11:61-68#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:61-68#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:61-68#2/r7.claim: Thamūd were ancient Arab inhabitants of Wādī al-Qurā between Medina and Syria; their traces are lost and little can be established about their history.
TABATABAI:11:61-68#2/r7.anchor: ثمود قوم من العرب العاربة كانوا يسكنون وادي القرى بين المدينة والشام

TABATABAI:11:61-68#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:61-68#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:61-68#2/r8.claim: The Quran portrays them as a later Arab nation with settled agriculture, plainside palaces, secure mountain homes, flowing springs, gardens, date palms, and crops.
TABATABAI:11:61-68#2/r8.anchor: ولهم حضارة ومدنية يعمرون الأرض ويتخذون من سهولها قصورا

TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r1.claim: Thamūd followed a tribal order led by notables and elders; nine men in the city where Salih was sent spread corruption, worshipped idols, and became excessively rebellious.
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r1.anchor: كانت ثمود تعيش على سنة الشعوب والقبائل يحكم فيهم سادتهم وشيوخهم وقد كانت في المدينة التي بعث فيها صالح تسعة رهط يفسدون

TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r2.claim: Salih came from a distinguished, respected family and was known for intelligence and competence; he called them to monotheism, abandon idols, justice, and restraint from arrogance and excess.
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r2.anchor: وكان من بيت الشرف والفخار معروفا بالعقل والكفاية فدعاهم إلى توحيد الله سبحانه وأن يتركوا عبادة الأصنام وأن يسيروا في مجتمعهم بالعدل والإحسان

TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r3.claim: Only a few weak people believed; the arrogant majority persisted in unbelief, humiliated believers, and called Salih foolish and a sorcerer.
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r3.anchor: فلم يؤمن به إلا جماعة قليلة من ضعفائهم وأما الطغاة المستكبرون وعامة من تبعهم فأصروا على كفرهم واستذلوا الذين آمنوا به

TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r6.claim: The city’s clans plotted to kill Salih and his family, then deny responsibility to their heir; God counter-plotted and struck them with the blast, quake, and cry, while saving the believers.
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r6.anchor: ثم مكرت شعوب المدينة وأرهاطها بصالح وتقاسموا بينهم لنبيتنه وأهله ثم نقولن لوليه ما شهدنا مهلك أهله

TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r7.claim: After destruction, Salih turned away reproaching them for rejecting his Lord’s message and counsel; the divine announcement declares Thamūd’s disbelief and ruin.
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r7.anchor: فتولى عنهم وقال يا قوم لقد أبلغتكم رسالة ربي ونصحت لكم ولكن لا تحبون الناصحين

TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r8.claim: The present Torah does not mention Salih; he is the third prophet in the Quranic sequence after Noah and Hūd, whom God praises and chooses above the worlds.
TABATABAI:11:61-68#3/r8.anchor: كان عليه السلام من قوم ثمود ثالث الأنبياء المذكورين في القرآن

TABRISI:11:61-68/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:61-68/r3.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:11:61-68/r3.claim: Sibawayh distinguishes names used for a people, tribe, or ancestor, and names whose use is evenly shared; Thamud and Saba belong to the last type.
TABRISI:11:61-68/r3.anchor: هو ثمود وسبأ فهما مرة للقبيلتين ومرة للحيين

TABRISI:11:68/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:68/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:68/r1.claim: Because Thamud equally denotes tribe and people, either declension or non-declension is acceptable, as is varying by position; al-Tabrisi says recitation must follow the transmitted readers.
TABRISI:11:68/r1.anchor: فمن صرف في جميع المواضع كان حسنا

TABRISI:11:68/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:68/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:68/r2.claim: The verse “a people of Taghlib” combines “people” with “daughter of Wa'il,” illustrating that a name can be used for both a community and its tribe.
TABRISI:11:68/r2.anchor: كسا الله حي تغلب ابنة وائل

TABRISI:11:68/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:68/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:68/r3.claim: Poetry and a hadith show “Yahud” as a tribe name and therefore uninflected; the same argument applies to “Majus,” which would be inflected if it named a people.
TABRISI:11:68/r3.anchor: فقد قامت الدلالة على أن يهود استعملت على أنها للقبيلة

TABRISI:11:68/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:68/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:68/r8.claim: “Ghaniya bi-l-makān” means to reside there and “al-maghnā” is a dwelling; al-Nabigha's line illustrates it. The root also denotes sufficiency, wealth, or song as a self-sufficient sound.
TABRISI:11:68/r8.anchor: وغني بالمكان إذا أقام به والمغنى المنزل قال النابغة

TABRISI:11:68#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:68#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:68#2/r1.claim: The explanation of the destruction formula here was already given in the account of ʿĀd.

TABRISI:11:68#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:68#2/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
TABRISI:11:68#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī supplies an omitted phrase: God rescued them from punishment and from the disgrace that clung to them that day.
TABRISI:11:68#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: هذا معطوف على محذوف تقديره نجيناهم من العذاب

TABRISI:11:68#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:68#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:68#2/r3.claim: Khizy is disgrace whose scandal becomes visible and which makes its sufferer ashamed.
TABRISI:11:68#2/r3.anchor: والخزي العيب الذي تظهر فضيحته ويستحي من مثله

TABRISI:11:68#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:68#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:68#2/r14.claim: They seemed never to have lived in their homes because destruction erased their traces, except for bodies that testified to their disgrace.
TABRISI:11:68#2/r14.anchor: لانقطاع آثارهم بالهلاك إلا ما بقي من أجسادهم الدالة على الخزي

TABRISI:11:68#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:68#2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:68#2/r15.claim: The closing declaration that Thamūd disbelieved and was banished is explained earlier in the commentary.
TABRISI:11:68#2/r15.anchor: ألا بعدا لثمود } قد سبق تفسيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r1.claim: The meaning of their seeming not to have lived there is explained in the commentary on al-A'raf.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r2.claim: The name Thamud is read either with declension or without: with declension when it names the masculine people, without it when it names the tribe.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r3.claim: Since Thamud can name either the tribe or its people and neither reading has an advantage, both declension and indeclinability are sound, as with Yahud and Majus.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي (¬1): فإذا استوى في ثمود أن تكون مرة للقبيلة ومرة للحي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r4.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r4.claim: An anonymous poet's line uses Yahud as a tribal name, supporting the indeclinable analysis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر (¬2): فرت يهود وأسلمت جيرانها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r5.speaker: الحديث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r5.claim: The hadith wording تقسم يهود likewise treats Yahud as a tribal name.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r6.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r6.claim: An anonymous poet uses Majus as a tribal name; if it referred only to people it would take declension.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r6.anchor: وقال آخر (¬4): كنار (¬5) مجوس تستعر استعارا

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:66/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:66/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:66/r1.claim: During the three-day respite, Saleh probably left with the believers and escaped; on the fourth day a loud blast destroyed Thamud.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:66/r1.anchor: muhtemelen Hz. Sâlih kendine inananlarla birlikte yurdu terkedip kurtuluşa erdi; dördüncü günde Allah’ın azabı geldi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:66/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:66/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:66/r2.claim: The use of rajfah, meaning earthquake, in place of sayha (“blast”) in 7:78 indicates that the destructive calamity was a noisy earthquake.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:66/r2.anchor: “korkunç ses” diye çevirilen sayha kelimesi yerine A‘râf sûresinde (7/78) “deprem” anlamına gelen recfe kelimesinin kullanılmış olmasından

ITQAN:v4p366/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p366/r1.speaker: نوف الشامي
ITQAN:v4p366/r1.claim: Nawf al-Shāmī says Ṣāliḥ was an Arab; after ʿĀd’s destruction Thamūd settled after them, and God sent Ṣāliḥ as a youth, who preached until old age; only Hūd and Ṣāliḥ were prophets between Noah and Abraham.
ITQAN:v4p366/r1.anchor: وقال نوف الشامي صالح من العرب لما أهلك الله عادا عمرت ثمود بعدها فبعث الله إليهم صالحا غلاما شابا

ITQAN:v4p366/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p366/r2.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v4p366/r2.claim: Ibn Ḥajar and others say the Qur’an indicates that Thamūd followed ʿĀd just as ʿĀd followed Noah.
ITQAN:v4p366/r2.anchor: وقال ابن حجر وغيره القرآن يدل على أن ثمودا كان بعد عاد كما كان عاد بعد قوم نوح

ITQAN:v4p366/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p366/r3.speaker: الثعلبي عن النووي
ITQAN:v4p366/r3.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī, quoting al-Nawawī’s Tahdhīb, gives Ṣāliḥ’s genealogy, says he was sent young to an Arab people between the Ḥijāz and Syria, stayed twenty years, and died in Mecca aged fifty-eight.
ITQAN:v4p366/r3.anchor: وقال الثعلبي ونقله عن النووي في تهذيبه ومن خطه نقلت هو صالح بن عبيد بن أسيف بن ماشج

ITQAN:v4p366/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p366/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p366/r9.claim: Mūsā is identified as son of ʿImrān through Yaʿqūb, with no disagreement reported about his lineage; his name is Syriac.
ITQAN:v4p366/r9.anchor: موسى هو ابن عمران يصهر بن قاهث بن لاوي بن يعقوب عليه السلام لاخلاف في نسبه وهو اسم سرياني

ITQAN:v4p366/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p366/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p366/r10.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says Mūsā was named for being cast between water and a tree: in Coptic, water is mū and tree is sā.
ITQAN:v4p366/r10.anchor: وأخرج أبو الشيخ من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال إنما سمى موسى لأنه ألقي بين شجر وماء

AKHFASH:v1p384/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p384/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p384/r4.claim: Thamūd is declined when understood as the people or their ancestor; the non-declined reading treats it as a feminine tribal name, but Akhfash reads the declined form and allows declension generally for a masculine people or ancestor name.
AKHFASH:v1p384/r4.anchor: وانما قرىء منه مصروفا ما كانت فيه الألف. وبذلك نقرأ.

FARRA:v2p20/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p20/r1.speaker: الأسود بن يزيد
FARRA:v2p20/r1.claim: Al-Aswad ibn Yazīd did not decline Thamūd anywhere in the Qurʾan, and Ḥamza followed this reading.
FARRA:v2p20/r1.anchor: عن أبيه أنه كان لا يجري (ثمود) في شيء من القرآن (فقرأ بذلك حمزة)

FARRA:v2p20/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p20/r2.speaker: الكسائي
FARRA:v2p20/r2.claim: Some readers decline Thamūd in the accusative because it is written with alif; al-Kisāʾī follows that in accusative but generally leaves it indeclinable in nominative and genitive.
FARRA:v2p20/r2.anchor: ومنهم من أجرى (ثمود) في النصب لأنها مكتوبة بالألف في كل القرآن إلا في موضع واحد

FARRA:v2p20/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p20/r3.speaker: الكسائي
FARRA:v2p20/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī exceptionally declines the second occurrence لثمود because it is close to the first; he considered differing case on the repeated word awkward.
FARRA:v2p20/r3.anchor: فأخذ بذلك الكسائي فأجراها في النصب ولم يجرها في الخفض ولا في الرفع

FARRA:v2p20/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p20/r4.speaker: جاء في التفسير
FARRA:v2p20/r4.claim: The exegetical gloss is كفروا نعمة ربهم; Arabic permits كفرتك and كفرت بك, as well as several constructions with شكر.
FARRA:v2p20/r4.anchor: جاء في التفسير: كفروا نعمة ربهم. والعرب تقول: كفرتك.

FARRA:v2p20/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p20/r5.speaker: الكسائي
FARRA:v2p20/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī heard Arabs say شكرت بالله, by analogy with كفرت بالله.
FARRA:v2p20/r5.anchor: وقال الكسائي: سمعت العرب تقول: شكرت بالله كقولهم: كفرت بالله.

SAMIN-DURR:11:68/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:68/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:68/r1.claim: Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ leave Thamūd diptote here and at 25:38, 29:38, and 53:51; Abū Bakr agrees only at 53:51.
SAMIN-DURR:11:68/r1.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وحفص: { ألا إن ثمود } هنا، وفي الفرقان:

SAMIN-DURR:11:68/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:68/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:68/r2.claim: All readers except al-Kisāʾī leave ثمود diptote in بعدا لثمود; those who do so treat it as a tribe name, while al-Kisāʾī declines it as the name of a people. Two unnamed poetic lines illustrate the forms.
SAMIN-DURR:11:68/r2.anchor: وقوله: { ألا بعدا لثمود } منعه القراء الصرف إلا الكسائي فإنه صرفه.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p483/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p483/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p483/r3.claim: The expression occurs of Madyan in al-A'raf and Hud, of Thamud in Hud, and with the same sense in the parable of worldly life in Yunus.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p483/r3.anchor: وفي المعنى نفسه، جاءت في مثل الحياة الدنيا بآية يونس 24

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.claim: When an accusative noun is followed by another coordinated noun, accusative is preferred if both are construed with the verb; Qur'anic examples include ثمودا, فريقا, and الظالمين.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.anchor: النصب ههنا لأن الاسم الأول مبنى على الفعل

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.claim: The same verb based accusative coordination works with كان and ليس, which behave like verbs in their government.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.anchor: ومثل ذلك كنت أخاك وزيدا كنت له أخا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.claim: Raising the second noun is also good when it begins an independent clause; it is more natural the closer that noun stands to the beginning.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.anchor: كأنك قلت لقيت زيدا وعمرو أفضل منه

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.claim: After ولكن or بل, the second noun follows the same accusative or permitted nominative patterns as a noun joined by ordinary conjunctions, since these particles govern nothing.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيت.anchor: لأن بل ولكن لا تعملان شيئا وتشركان الآخر مع الأول

IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r2.claim: These readers tanwīn-decline Thamūd in four locations but leave it indeclinable in ألا بعدا لثمود.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r2.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر بالتنوين فى أربعة مواضع فى هود / ألا إن ثمودا /

IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r3.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r3.claim: Hamza leaves Thamūd indeclinable in all five occurrences; al-Kisāʾī declines all five.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بترك صرف هذه الأحرف الخمسة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r4.speaker: الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī declines all five occurrences of Thamūd.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r5.speaker: يحيى بن آدم عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r5.claim: Yahya ibn Adam reports Abu Bakr declining the three occurrences in Hud, al-Furqān, and al-ʿAnkabūt, but not al-Najm; other reports from Abu Bakr decline four, while Hafs leaves all indeclinable.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p336/r5.anchor: روى يحيى بن آدم عن أبى بكر عنه أنه أجرى ثمودا فى ثلاثة مواضع فى هود والفرقان والعنكبوت

NASHR:v2p290/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p290/r1.speaker: الكسائي والباقون
NASHR:v2p290/r1.claim: Al-Kisai reads the dāl in بعدا with kasra and tanwin; the other readers use fatḥa without tanwin.
NASHR:v2p290/r1.anchor: فقرأ الكسائي بكسر الدال مع التنوين

NASHR:v2p289/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p289/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p289/r9.claim: Yaʿqūb, Ḥamza, and Ḥafṣ read Thamūd without tanwīn in all four locations; Abū Bakr joins them at the Najm location, while the other readers use tanwīn.
NASHR:v2p289/r9.anchor: يعقوب، وحمزة وحفص ثمود في الأربعة، وبغير تنوين

NASHR:v2p289/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p289/r10.speaker: أبو علي العطار
NASHR:v2p289/r10.claim: A unique route through Abū ʿAlī al-ʿAṭṭār transmits two faces at the Najm occurrence, one without tanwīn and one with it.
NASHR:v2p289/r10.anchor: وانفرد أبو علي العطار شيخ ابن سوار عن الكناني عن الحربي عن ابن عون عن الصريفيني عن يحيى عنه فيه بوجهين، أحدهما عدم التنوين، والثاني بالتنوين

NASHR:v2p289/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p289/r11.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p289/r11.claim: Readers who use tanwīn stop with alif, while those without tanwīn stop without it; one exceptional route from Ḥafṣ stops with alif despite no tanwīn.
NASHR:v2p289/r11.anchor: وكل من نون وقف بالألف، ومن لم ينون وقف بغير ألف

NASHR:v2p143/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p143/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p143/r3.claim: For ثمود without tanwīn in Hūd, al-Furqān, al-ʿAnkabūt, and al-Najm, the author defers discussion of the stopping form to the Hūd section.
NASHR:v2p143/r3.anchor: وأما ثمود من قوله تعالى: ألا إن ثمود في هود وعادا وثمود في الفرقان، وفي العنكبوت والنجم

QIRAAT-ER:11:68:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:68:7#1/r1.speaker: CE
QIRAAT-ER:11:68:7#1/r1.claim: Tanwīn treats Thamūd as triptote and a masculine Arabic noun rather than a diptote foreign or tribal proper name.
QIRAAT-ER:11:68:7#1/r1.anchor: Tanwīn added (ثَمُودًا vs ثَمُودَ) — treating the name as fully declinable (triptote/munṣarif) rather than diptote

QIRAAT-ER:11:68:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:68:13#1/r1.speaker: CE
QIRAAT-ER:11:68:13#1/r1.claim: Genitive tanwīn treats Thamūd as fully declinable and suggests an Arabic-origin noun rather than a foreign proper name.
QIRAAT-ER:11:68:13#1/r1.anchor: Genitive tanwīn (li-Thamūdin vs li-Thamūda) — treating the name as triptote/fully declinable

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p178/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p178/r5.speaker: حمزة وحفص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p178/r5.claim: Hamza and Hafs leave ثمود in إن ثمود undeclined; the other readers decline it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p178/r5.anchor: ألا إن ثمود، منع حمزة وحفص صرفه، وصرفه الباقون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p178/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p178/r6.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p178/r6.claim: Al-Kisaʾi declines ثمود after ل; the others of the seven leave it undeclined.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r1.claim: They seemed never to have lived or remained in their homes, as though they had never existed there.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r2.claim: Some parse the clause as a circumstantial phrase describing their state after becoming prostrate corpses.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r2.anchor: والجملة قيل : في موضع الحال أي أصبحوا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r3.claim: Replacing the pronoun with Thamūd makes the identity of the condemned people explicit.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r4.speaker: حفص وحمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r4.claim: Ḥafṣ and Ḥamza leave Thamūd diptotic, treating it as the tribe's name.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r4.anchor: ومنعه من الصرف حفص وحمزة نظرا إلى القبيلة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r5.speaker: أكثر السبعة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r5.claim: Most of the Seven reciters declinate Thamūd, regarding it as the people rather than the tribe.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r5.anchor: وصرفه أكثر السبعة نظرا إلى الحي كما قدمنا آنفا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r6.claim: Another explanation takes Thamūd as the primordial ancestor, requiring an understood descendant or offspring; another says its earlier form explains declension even though it denotes the tribe here.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r6.anchor: وقيل : نظرا إلى الأب الأكبر يعني يكون المراد به الأب الأول وهو مصروف وحينئذ يقدر مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r7.claim: Explicitly naming their disbelief, though already evident, censures them and explains the prayer for their ruin.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r7.anchor: صرح بكفرهم مع كونه معلوما مما سبق من أحوالهم تقبيحا لحالهم وتعليلا لإستحقاقهم الدعاء عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r8.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p92#3/r8.claim: Al-Kisāʾī alone reads the name with tanwīn.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p187#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p187#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p187#2/r1.claim: The phrase means that they had not lived or stayed there.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p187#2/r1.anchor: كأن لم يغنوا فيها} يقيموا ويكونوا فيها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p187#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p187#2/r2.speaker: حمزة وحفص ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p187#2/r2.claim: Ḥamza, Ḥafṣ, and Yaʿqūb read Thamūd without tanwīn here and in al-Furqān, al-ʿAnkabūt, and al-Najm; Abū Bakr agrees in al-Najm, while the other readers use tanwīn.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p187#2/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة وحفص ويعقوب: "ثمود" غير منون، وكذلك في سورة الفرقان والعنكبوت والنجم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p187#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p187#2/r3.speaker: الكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p187#2/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the dāl of لثمود with kasra and tanwīn, while the others read it with fatḥ and no tanwīn; the declined form treats it as a masculine personal name, the indeclinable form as a tribal name.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p187#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي: "لثمود" بخفض الدال والتنوين، والباقون بنصب الدال، فمن جره فلأنه اسم مذكر

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:66-68/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:66-68/r5.speaker: أبو بكر والكسائي وابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:66-68/r5.claim: Authorities vary in tanwīn on Thamūd here, in al-Najm, and in the later curse; the choice treats the name as the tribe or founding ancestor.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:66-68/r5.anchor: نونه أبو بكر ها هنا وفي «النجم» والكسائي في جميع القرآن وابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو

BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r8.claim: Juthūm is a euphemism for death; saying they became so by morning heightens the terror and regret of their sudden stillness as though they had never existed.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r8.anchor: ولما كان الجثوم كناية عن الموت أوضحه بقوله

BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r9.claim: The phrase depicts them as having vanished without a trace; ghana can suggest living in prosperity and song, while al-maghānī means dwellings and the root sense is sufficiency.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r11.claim: Alā is an alerting formula used for momentous matters, meant to keep a heedless listener from overlooking what follows.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r11.anchor: مفتتحا بالأداة التي لا تقال إلا عندالأمور الهائلة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r12.speaker: الرماني
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r12.claim: Al-Rummani analyzes alā as the interrogative alif entering lā: together they produce an alerting sense through affirmation and negation.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r12.anchor: قال الرماني : وهي ألف الاستفهام دخلت على ( لا ) فالألف تقتضي معنى , و ( لا ) تنفي معنى

BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r13.claim: Biqaʿi explains lā as negating what follows and the interrogative denial as negating lā; the double negation affirms the point especially emphatically.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r13.anchor: أن ( لا ) دخلت على ما بعدها فنفته , ثم دخلت عليها همزة الإنكار فنفتها , ومن المعلوم أن نفي النفي إثبات

BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r14.claim: The declinable reading of Thamud signals contempt for their rash disobedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r14.anchor: قراءة الصرف دالة علىالاستخفاف بهم لطيشهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r15.claim: They covered over their Lord, their benefactor through creation, provision, and sending, as well as His attributes and acts.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r15.anchor: أوقعوا التغطية والستر على المحسن غليهم بالخلق والرزق

BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r16.claim: Making kafarū transitive directly to their Lord, unlike many parallels, marks the coarseness of their unbelief.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r16.anchor: فإيصال الفعل دون قصره كما في أكثر أضرابه بيان لغلظة كفرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r17.speaker: غير الكسائي
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r17.claim: Readers other than al-Kisaʾi leave Thamud indeclinable here, signaling their lasting banishment and distance.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r17.anchor: ترك صرفهم في قراءة غير الكسائي إيذانا بدوام لبثهم في الطرد والبعد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r18.claim: Repeating alā confirms the condemnation and announces the permanence of their destruction.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r18.anchor: ثم كرر ذلك تأكيدا له وإعلاما بتأبيد هلاكهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r19.claim: Thamud may be declined when it names the tribe’s father and left indeclinable when it names the tribe; declension in the accusative was chosen for lightness.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r19.anchor: لما جاز الصرف في ثمود باعتبار أنه اسم أبي القبيلة وعدمه باعتبار إطلاقه على القبيلة اختير الصرف في النصب فقط لخفته

DURR-FULL:v4p445/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as though they had never lived there.
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {كأن لم يغنوا فيها} قال: كأن لم يعيشوا فيها

DURR-FULL:v4p445/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r5.claim: A second Ibn Abbas gloss says it was as if they had never dwelt there.
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس {كأن لم يغنوا فيها} قال: كأن لم يعمروا فيها

DURR-FULL:v4p445/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r6.claim: To Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq, Ibn Abbas explains that they seemed never to have existed or lived in the world when punished.
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله عز وجل

DURR-FULL:v4p445/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r7.speaker: لبيد بن ربيعة
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas cites Labid ibn Rabiʿa’s use of «غنيت» as evidence for the sense of dwelling or living.
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r7.anchor: لبيد بن ربيعة وهو يقول: وغنيت شيئا قبل نحري وأحسن لو كان للنفس اللجوج خلود

DURR-FULL:v4p445/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r8.claim: Qatada glosses it as if they had never enjoyed life there.
DURR-FULL:v4p445/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {كأن لم يغنوا فيها} قال: كأن لم ينعموا فيها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as if they had never inhabited the place.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : كان لم يغنوا فيها قال : كان لم يعمروا فيها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r2.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas says they had not lived there.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : كان لم يغنوا فيها يقول : لم يعيشوا فيها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r3.claim: Qatada says they had not enjoyed or prospered there.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة كان لم يغنوا فيها كان لم ينعموا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r4.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r4.claim: Abu Malik explains it as though they had never been there.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2052#2/r4.anchor: وروي عن أبي مالك كان لم يكونوا فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r1.claim: Ibn Ashur points to analogous material in the account of Hud in al-Araf and notes that Shuayb was discussed there earlier.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r1.anchor: تقدم الكلام على نظائر بعض هذه الآية في قصة هود في سورة الأعراف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r9.claim: The phrase means that they had never lived there.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r10.claim: Most readers use tanwin, treating Thamud as the ancestor's name; Hamza, Hafs from Asim, and Yaqub omit it, treating Thamud as the people or tribe. Both are established Arab treatments of tribal names derived from ancestors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r10.anchor: على اعتبار ثمود اسم جد الأمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r11.claim: Ibn Ashur refers to the earlier discussion of بعدا in Noah's story at 11:44.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p114#4/r11.anchor: وتقدم الكلام على { بعدا } في قصة نوح { وقيل بعدا للقوم الظالمين } ( هود : 44 )

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r6.claim: Yaghnaw means they lived in a place in ease; maghānī refers to dwellings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r6.anchor: ويغنوا مضارع من غني في المكان إذا أقام فيه في خفض عيش وهي المغاني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r7.speaker: حمزة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r7.claim: Ḥamza alone leaves Thamūd undeclined in this verse and in al-Furqān, al-ʿAnkabūt, and al-Najm; al-Kisāʾī declines it throughout those passages.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وحده: «ألا ان ثمود» وكذلك في الفرقان والعنكبوت والنجم، وصرفها الكسائي كلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r8.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r8.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim leaves Thamūd undeclined in ألا بعدا لثمود, like Ḥamza.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r8.anchor: واختلف عن عاصم: فروى عنه حفص ترك الإجراء كحمزة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r9.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r9.claim: Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim declines Thamūd in the other three occurrences but leaves it undeclined in ألا بعدا لثمود.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r9.anchor: وروى عنه أبو بكر إجراء الأربعة وتركه في قوله: ألا بعدا لثمود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r10.speaker: باقي القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r10.claim: The remaining readers decline Thamūd in ألا إن ثمودا but leave it undeclined after ألا بعدا; both forms are eloquent and they decline it in al-Furqān, al-ʿAnkabūt, and al-Najm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p186#2/r10.anchor: والقراءتان فصيحتان وكذلك صرفوا في الفرقان والعنكبوت والنجم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Nāfiʿ, and Ibn ʿĀmir use tanwīn at four of the five cited occurrences, but leave it off in this phrase.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ ألا بعدا لثمود ﴾ اختلفوا في صرف ثمود وترك إجرائه في خمسة مواضع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r2.speaker: حمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r2.claim: Ḥamza leaves the noun without tanwīn in all five cited occurrences.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بترك صرف هذه الخمسة الأحرف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r3.speaker: الكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī uses tanwīn in all five cited occurrences.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r4.speaker: حسين الجعفي عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r4.claim: Al-Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī reports that Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim inflected four of the occurrences like Abū ʿAmr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r4.anchor: روى حسين الجعفي عن أبي بكر عنه أنه أجرى الأربعة الأحرف مثل أبي عمرو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r5.speaker: يحيى بن آدم عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r5.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam reports that ʿĀṣim inflected three occurrences: Hūd 69, al-Furqān 38, and al-ʿAnkabūt 38.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r5.anchor: وروى يحيى بن آدم أنه أجرى ثلاثة في ( هود 69 )

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r6.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r6.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim leaves tanwīn off all five occurrences, like Ḥamza.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r6.anchor: وروى حفص عنه أنه لم يجر شيئا منها مثل حمزة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r7.claim: Thamūd is uninflected when it denotes the tribe, but takes tanwīn when it denotes the living community.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r7.anchor: واعلم أن ثمودا يراد به القبيلة تارة ويراد به الحي تارة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r8.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī directs readers to earlier explanations of material omitted here at al-Aʿrāf 73 and al-Tawba 70.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p126#3/r8.anchor: وما أخللنا به فقد سبق تفسيره ( الأعراف 73 والتوبة 70 ) إلى قوله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p332/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p332/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p332/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says the account of Salih and Thamud has already been covered fully in Surat al-A'raf, so he does not repeat it here.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p332/r1.anchor: وتقدم الكلام على هذه القصة مستوفى في سورة "الأعراف" (5) بما أغنى عن إعادته ها هنا

JISHUMI:v5p3525/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r4.speaker: حمزة، وحفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r4.claim: Hamza and Hafs from Asim read Thamud without tanwin throughout the Quran.
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة، وحفص عن عاصم: ألا إن ثمود غير منون كل القرآن

JISHUMI:v5p3525/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r5.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r5.claim: The remaining readers use tanwin here and at the cited occurrences in al-Furqan, al-Ankabut, and al-Najm because the word is written with alif in those places; Abu Bakr from Asim does not use tanwin at al-Najm.
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r5.anchor: وقرأ الباقون ثمودا بالتنوين ههنا، وفي (الفرقان)، و(العنكبوت)، و(النجم)؛ لأنه مكتوب بالألف في هذه المواضع

JISHUMI:v5p3525/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r6.speaker: الكسائي
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r6.claim: Al-Kisa'i alone reads بعدا لثمود in the genitive with tanwin; al-Farra reports his explanation that it is near the accusative and therefore مجزئ.
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r6.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي وحده: ألا بعدا لثمود بالخفض والتنوين، قال الفراء: قلت له: لم ذاك؟ قال: لأنه قرب من المنصوب، وهو مجزئ

JISHUMI:v5p3525/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r7.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r7.claim: The other readers give the word fatḥa without tanwin; the author says either declension is permitted in the accusative.
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r7.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح الدال غير منونة، وقد بينا أنه يجوز صرفه وترك صرفه في المنصوب.

JISHUMI:v5p3525/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r12.claim: To dwell in a place means to remain there; dwellings are called maghani because people find sufficiency in them, while the root ghina denotes sufficiency.
JISHUMI:v5p3525/r12.anchor: وغنى بالمكان: أقام به، ومنه: المغاني: المنازل، سميت بذلك لاكتفاء الناس بها؛ لأن أصل الغنى الكفاية.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r11.claim: The phrase can mean it was as if they had never lived there.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r12.claim: Alternatively, it was as if they had never enjoyed its prosperity.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r13.claim: One gloss is that Thamūd denied their Lord’s threat.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r14.claim: Another gloss is that they disbelieved God’s command.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r15.claim: The destruction annihilated Thamūd except Abū Ramḥān, who was in God’s sanctuary and was protected from the punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r15.anchor: إلا رجلا منهم وهو أبو رمحان كان في حرم الله تعالى فمنعه الحرم

MUQATIL:11:68/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:68/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:68/r1.claim: The phrase means that the people of Thamud seemed never to have lived in this world.
MUQATIL:11:68/r1.anchor: كأنهم لم يكونوا في الدنيا قط

MUQATIL:11:68/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:68/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:68/r2.claim: Thamud disbelieved in the oneness of their Lord, and the prayer that they be far away refers to their destruction.
MUQATIL:11:68/r2.anchor: ألا إن ثمود كفروا } بتوحيد { ربهم ألا بعدا لثمود

NASAFI-FULL:v2p163#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p163#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p163#2/r1.claim: The phrase means they had not dwelt there.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p163#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p163#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p163#2/r2.claim: Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ read Thamūd with declension, which can refer to the people or ancestor; indeclinability treats it as a feminine tribal name.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p163#2/r2.anchor: ثمود حمزة وحفص ﴿ ألا بعدا لثمود ﴾ فالصرف للذهاب إلى الحى أو الأب الأكبر ومنعه للتعريف والتأنيث بمعنى القبيلة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p163#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p163#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p163#2/r3.claim: He invokes distance and ruin for Thamūd.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p163#2/r3.anchor: فالصرف للذهاب إلى الحى أو الأب الأكبر ومنعه للتعريف

QURTUBI-FULL:11:67-68/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:67-68/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:67-68/r4.claim: He says the closing declaration that Thamud disbelieved and were banished was explained earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:67-68/r4.anchor: { ألا إن ثمود كفروا ربهم ألا بعدا لثمود } تقدم معناه

BURSEVI:v4p100/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p100/r1.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v4p100/r1.claim: Bahr al-ʿUlūm explains جثم as sitting motionless and silent, and مجثمة as an animal tied with its legs gathered so it can be shot.
BURSEVI:v4p100/r1.anchor: قال في بحر العلوم : يقال : الناس جثم ، أي : قعود لاحراك بهم ولا ينبسون بنبسة ومنه المجثمة التي نهى الشرع عنها

BURSEVI:v4p100/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p100/r2.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v4p100/r2.claim: The Mathnawi's image of kneeling under divine punishment illustrates جاثمين as crouched or brought to one's knees.
BURSEVI:v4p100/r2.anchor: وفي المثنوى : شحنه قهر خدا ايشان بجست خونبهاى اشترى شهري درست

BURSEVI:v4p100/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p100/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p100/r3.claim: They appear as though they had never inhabited their homes or lived and moved about there.
BURSEVI:v4p100/r3.anchor: أي : كأنهم لم يقيموا في ديارهم ولم يكونوا أحياء مترددين متصرفين وهو في موقع الحال

BURSEVI:v4p100/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p100/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p100/r4.claim: The clause functions as a circumstantial phrase: they became crouched as if they had never existed or stayed anywhere.
BURSEVI:v4p100/r4.anchor: وهو في موقع الحال أي : أصبحوا جاثمين مماثلين لمن لم يوجد ولم يقم في مقام قط.

BURSEVI:v4p100/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p100/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p100/r5.claim: مغنى means a home or place of residence; غنى بالمكان means to reside there, and غنى alone can mean to live.
BURSEVI:v4p100/r5.anchor: والمغنى المنزل والمقام الذي يقيم الحي به يقال : غنى الرجل بمكان كذا ، أي : أقام به وغنى أي : عاش.

BURSEVI:v4p100/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p100/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p100/r6.claim: The warning says Thamud denied God's oneness and cautions later peoples.
BURSEVI:v4p100/r6.anchor: إن ثمود كفروا ربهم جحدوا بوحدانية الله تعالى فهذا تنبيه وتخويف لمن بعدهم

BURSEVI:v4p100/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p100/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p100/r7.claim: بعدا is a verbal noun used in place of its verb, meaning that Thamud perished; the lām identifies the people cursed.
BURSEVI:v4p100/r7.anchor: فقولهبعدا مصدر وضع موضع فعله فإن معناه بعدوا اي هلكوا ، واللام لبيان من دعى عليهم

BURSEVI:v4p100/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p100/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p100/r8.claim: The curse after their death underscores that they deserved annihilating punishment for disbelief, denial, and hamstringing God's she-camel.
BURSEVI:v4p100/r8.anchor: وفائدة الدعاء عليهم بعد هلاكهم الدلالة على استحقاقهم عذاب

BURSEVI:v4p100/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p100/r9.speaker: جابر
BURSEVI:v4p100/r9.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet's Tabuk sermon: do not ask for signs like Salih's people; the she-camel drank on her day and gave milk on theirs, but they rebelled, received a three-day warning, and were destroyed except Abu Righal sheltered in the sanctuary.
BURSEVI:v4p100/r9.anchor: وعن جابر رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله لما نزل الحجر في غزوة تبوك قام فخطب الناس فقال : يا أيها الناس لا تسألوا نبيكم الآيات

BURSEVI:v4p100/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p100/r10.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v4p100/r10.claim: The destruction signifies the soul and its traits being struck by separation; those who take refuge in the sanctuary of Sacred Law gain nearness and Paradise.
BURSEVI:v4p100/r10.anchor: الإشارة فيه أنه أشار إلى إهلاك النفس وصفاتها بعذاب البعد وصاعقة القهر إلا ما كان في حرم الله تعالى وهو الشريعة

RAZI-FULL:v18p18/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p18/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p18/r9.claim: The phrase means it is as if they had never existed there: al-maghnā is a dwelling place, and غني بالمكان means to reside there.
RAZI-FULL:v18p18/r9.anchor: والمغنى المقام الذي يقيم الحي به

RAZI-FULL:v18p19/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p19/r1.speaker: حمزة وحفص عن عاصم والباقون
RAZI-FULL:v18p19/r1.claim: Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read Thamūd without tanwīn throughout the Qur'an, while the other readers use tanwīn; declension treats the name as a people or forefather, while indeclinability treats it as the feminine tribe name.
RAZI-FULL:v18p19/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة وحفص عن عاصم { ألا إن ثمود } غير منون في كل القرآن ، وقرأ الباقون { * ثمودا } بالتنوين
